website.faq.page-subtitle: Common issues and fixes for Firestone.
website.faq.sections.app-isnt-showing.bo:
• Make sure Overwolf is running before you launch Hearthstone
  • Check that the Overwolf overlay is enabled: Overwolf game settings
  • Run Firestone as admin (you'll have to close Overwolf and reopen it afterwards). See Memory Reading Error / Run as admin
  • Check if you can access https://static.firestoneapp.com/data/i18n/enUS.json from Chrome. If not, this means that there is an issue with your router / ISP / VPN that blocks access to AWS. Parental control is also a known cause for this issue.
    • IMPORTANT: this seems to be a more prevalent cause of issues recently, so please check your parental control settings (also with your ISP), and whitelist https://static.zerotoheroes.com and https://static.firestoneapp.com
    • Also see the connectivity issues section at the bottom of this page
  • It has been found out that DirectX 12 can interfere with the overlay rendering. Try to disable it to see if it improves the situation (TODO: detailed instructions needed)
  • If everything fails, and if your game is installed under C:\Program Files or C:\Program Files (x86), try moving the game to another folder. These folders are protected and might cause some issue when the app tries to read the game's information
website.faq.sections.check-if-running-as: Check if the app is running as admin
website.faq.sections.connectivity-issues:
• Try to disable your antivirus / firewall / VPN
  • If you know how to, whitelist the following domains:
    • zerotoheroes.com
    • firestoneapp.com
    • amazonaws.com
    • overwolf.com
  • Reinstalling Firestone sometimes seems to help
website.faq.sections.dns.title: DNS
website.faq.sections.game-is-crashing.bo:
• See this Blizzard forum thread. You need to add the -force-d3d11 parameter, as shown in this screenshot:
  • There can be issues with RivaTuner / MSI AfterBurner. See Overwolf and conflicts with RivaTuner
  • If you're using AMD, you can try disabling AMD Fluid Motion Frames 2
  • One user reported that the game would crash in windowed mode, but not in fullscreen.
  • Overwolf does not yet support ARM processors, and running it on an ARM processor machine can cause the game to crash
website.faq.sections.game-is-slow-high-r:
Capping the game at 60 FPS can make high-APM play feel sluggish. A better alternative on a high-refresh monitor is to cap slightly below the refresh rate and keep variable refresh working:

  • Set the game and GPU frame limiter to your monitor's refresh rate minus 6 (for example, 144 Hz → 138 FPS)
  • Keep G-Sync or FreeSync enabled and working
  • In NVIDIA Control Panel or NVIDIA Profile Inspector, set Vertical Sync to Fast Sync

Typical NVIDIA Profile Inspector values for a 144 Hz display:

  • Frame Rate Limiter V3: 138 FPS
  • GSYNC - Application Mode: Fullscreen and Windowed
  • GSYNC - Application State: Allow
  • GSYNC - Global Feature: On
  • GSYNC - Global Mode: Fullscreen and Windowed
  • Vertical Sync: Fast Sync
website.faq.sections.game-is-slow.body:
• If the game experiences some stuttering / "choppy" animations while Firestone is running, you can try capping the game's FPS.
    • To do so, edit the options.txt file in %localappdata%\Blizzard\Hearthstone and change / add targetframerate=60 to something lower (I use 60, others use 140 with success as well)
  • Some users have found that turning off G-Sync through the graphics card helps

  • I have AMD GPU and I just switch off AMD FreeSync in HS and there is no more lagging.
website.faq.sections.game-is-slow.title: Game is slow
website.faq.sections.general-checklist.b:
• Make sure Overwolf is running before you launch Hearthstone
  • (Especially after a new patch) Close HS, close Firestone, restart Firestone, restart HS. This will force the app update (updating while the game is running does not always work well)
  • Check if you can launch Firestone on the desktop (meaning when HS is not running). If nothing happens:
    • Please check the other sections below (most notably the ones at the bottom of this page about connectivity issues)
    • If nothing helps, please create a log zip and send it to me manually (on Discord for instance). See how to get your Overwolf logs
  • Check (while HS is running) whether you have a Decks.log file in your Hearthstone install folder under Logs/Hearthstone_XXX. If not, reboot HS
  • Try disabling your antivirus / firewall, and restart Firestone
  • If Firestone is flashing / blinking, it could be an issue with a new Lenovo app called LegionZone. Try deactivating it to see if it solves the issue.
  • Check that your in-game clock indicates the correct time. This can happen if your system time is not configured properly, typically the "Adjust for daylight saving time automatically" option is deactivated
website.faq.sections.high-resource-usage: • Some users have reported high GPU usage, which was caused by the Outplayed app. If that happens, try to deactivate that app
website.faq.sections.login-opens-overwol:
The website signs you back into the desktop app with a firestoneapp:// link. Overwolf also registers that protocol, so Windows can launch Overwolf even if you already quit it.

  • Open Windows Settings → Apps → Default apps
  • Search for Firestone Standalone, or for the protocol firestoneapp
  • Set Firestone Standalone as the default handler

Closing Overwolf does not unregister the protocol. Firestone Standalone re-registers firestoneapp:// each time it starts, but Windows may still prefer Overwolf until you change the default app.
Login opens Overwolf instead of Firestone Standalone
website.faq.sections.mainland-china.titl: 对于中国大陆用户 - For users from mainland China
website.faq.sections.memory-reading-erro:
• Close HS
  • Close Overwolf
  • Change Firestone and/or Overwolf shortcuts to "run as admin"
    • Overwolf.exe and OverwolfLauncher.exe should be run as admin
    • You can also activate the "apply to all users" button

• Restart Overwolf (some users had to restart their full computer)
  • Then you can restart HS
  • If it still doesn't work (even after a full computer restart), check if Hearthstone itself is running as admin. If it is, try to run it without admin privileges.
  • If you're still having issues, you can try to grant all permissions in that screen:
Memory Reading Error / Run as admin
website.faq.sections.memory-reading-othe:
• You can also try to run sfc /scannow in a command prompt, as this has solved the issue for at least 2 players
  • "Manually ending all processes related to hearthstone, bnet, overwolf, firestone, etc and then relaunching hs and firestone seems to have fixed it. A regular restart of hearthstone and overwolf/firestone via the system tray didn't"
  • One user managed to solve this issue by installing Overwolf in the same subdirectory as Hearthstone (like D:\Blizzard\HS\Hearthstone and D:\Blizzard\HS\Overwolf), so might be worth a try
Other things to try if you have the "Memory reading" error
